solutions.title: Solutions for Perfect New York, in order.
solutions.line: Shelter first, because every other standard is harder to reach without a home.

items.challenge: 145,560 New Yorkers had no home on one night in January 2025.
items.advises: Issue a State housing bond whose investors are repaid in part on outcomes: each household moved from shelter into a permanent home, building on New York’s own Pay for Success record. With super intelligence, New York can match every family in shelter to a vacant or buildable home and report each outcome as it happens.

items.challenge: computed:food of households were food insecure in 2022–2024, and computed:poverty of New Yorkers lived below the poverty line in 2025.
items.advises: Back a statewide social bond for food and income programs, priced off the State’s credit and paid against measured falls in hunger, county by county, starting with the Bronx. With super intelligence, the State can see where families are falling behind and reach them before they do.

items.challenge: computed:reading of fourth graders read at the NAEP Proficient level in 2024.
items.advises: Fund early reading through an outcome contract that pays only for measured gains, as the State first did for jobs in 2013. With super intelligence, every child can have a reading tutor that adapts to them, in their own language.

solutions.hold: Phase 3, hold the line: health coverage (computed:uninsured uninsured), with water and energy measured next.

capital.title: New York already finances at scale.
capital.line: Four instruments on record that a Perfect New York can build on.

items.name: MTA green bonds
items.line: Climate Bonds Certified green bonds issued by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority since 2016.

items.name: The Environmental Bond Act
items.line: Bonds for clean water, clean air and green jobs, approved by New York voters on 8 November 2022.

items.name: NY Green Bank
items.line: Committed to clean energy since 2013 by the State’s own green investment fund, supporting up to $10.4bn of projects.

items.name: Pay for Success
items.line: The nation’s first state-led Pay for Success project: private investors paid upfront for job training for formerly incarcerated New Yorkers; the State repays on results.
